transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Equinox Head of Product), Tom Alvarez (Platform Engineer), Jada Rivers (Security Lead)

Summary:
Quick discovery to validate fit for Redwood self-serve hosted API and clarify security requirements if Equinox moves to a pilot. Discussed time-to-first-token, free credits, expected throughput, and whether Dedicated or Private could be necessary later.

[00:00] Sophie Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick check — audio okay?
[00:08] Maya Chen: yeah good here, thanks Sophie. excited to dig in.
[00:12] Ravi Patel: morning/afternoon all — ravi here from the se side, i'll cover the quickstart flow and some perf notes.
[00:18] Tom Alvarez: tom — platform eng. i'm mostly curious about network egress, VPC peering, and how fast we can get our devs to make first requests.
[00:25] Jada Rivers: and i'm jada, security. SOC 2 is table stakes for us, also wondering about audit logs and key management.

Topics
[00:40] Sophie: goal for today is simple: make sure the self-serve path fits for your POC and to map security requirements. also i'll confirm credits and timeline so you can hit a first token quickly.

Transcript body
[01:05] Maya: high level — Equinox is building in-app intelligent search and a summarization layer for customer support docs. initially it's product-driven, small alpha for 5 power users, then expand to 100 users if metrics look good.
[01:22] Sophie: great, that sounds like a classic fast-path PLG use case. do you have an initial latency requirement? like p95 under 500ms or is that relaxed?
[01:30] Maya: for the alpha, 800-1s is fine. by beta we want 300-400ms p95 for short prompts. cost is important too; we want predictable spend.
[01:40] Ravi: couple things to call out — our hosted Redwood API will give you immediate watts to start — sorry, i said watts — immediate access, and we provide a free credit pool to get to first token. for lower unit-cost at scale you can move to Dedicated which is reserved GPU capacity, or to Private for on-prem/VPC if you need data residency.
[01:58] Tom: can you clarify the quickstart? how long to first token from sign-up, roughly?
[02:05] Sophie: typical is under 15 minutes if you follow the quickstart — we send org invite, you create an api key, sdk snippet, and you can hit /v1/generate. we'll drop in a little sample app repo.
[02:18] Tom: great. what about streaming? we need partial tokens for the UI.
[02:25] Ravi: yes streaming is supported in hosted. caveat: for very high concurrency we recommend batching and prefix caching (kv cache) which reduces cost. note — sometimes the transcript generator says KV "cash" in our notes so ignore that.

Security/perf questions
[02:40] Jada: SOC 2 — do you have a compliance pack? are there audit logs for every token request? retention?
[02:48] Sophie: we have a SOC 2 report and a security packet, i'll share the latest artifacts. audit logs: hosted includes request-level metadata and an optional full payload log for debugging; retention tiers are configurable via the console (30/90/365 days) — default is 90.
[03:10] Jada: is payload encryption customer-controlled? where are keys stored?
[03:15] Ravi: we integrate with KMS providers — HSM-backed KMS for enterprise. by default keys are managed by Redwood for the self-serve experience, but for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS. we'll note that in the security doc.
[03:30] Tom: network — our infra team doesn't want data traversing public internet. can we do VPC peering with hosted?
[03:38] Sophie: hosted doesn't currently do customer VPC peering; that's for Private. however we offer private dedicated edges in some regions and VPN tunnels for enterprise customers. for quickstart, traffic goes over TLS to Redwood endpoints.
[03:55] Maya: ok that may be fine for alpha. cost question — you mentioned credits, how many and what's the expiry?
[04:02] Sophie: we can issue 60 credits tied to your trial org (roughly ~60k tokens depending on model). expiration typically 90 days for PLG credits. we also include usage dashboards to track token split by route.

On Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private
[04:20] Ravi: wanted to map scenarios — hosted is fastest to ship, Dedicated when you need capacity predictability and lower per-token pricing, Private when you need VPC/on-prem or strict residency. most teams start hosted self-serve, then later adopt Dedicated if throughput/cost mix requires it.
[04:39] Maya: what sort of commit for Dedicated?
[04:42] Ravi: committed monthly or annual capacity, different GPU pools. pricing varies by model and quantization profile. we'll share a sample pricing matrix.
[04:50] Tom: and can we switch models without changing the app?
[04:53] Sophie: yes — routing layer supports model aliases and fallbacks so you can pin versions per route and rollback if needed. it's an API level setting.

Mis-transcriptions and clarifications
[05:05] Maya: you said KV cash earlier — yes that's fine — just making sure caching doesn't break context.
[05:11] Ravi: right it's KV cache, used to speed up decoding for repeated prefixes. small correction: in early notes we sometimes see "Redwood Dedicated" spelled as "Redwood Dedi" in our auto transcripts.

Pilot acceptance criteria
[05:20] Maya: our internal success metrics for alpha: function correctness of summarization (human-eval), latency under 1s p95, and cost under $X per 1k requests. we also need an audit log for every mutation.
[05:32] Jada: plus we need SSO with SAML and RBAC control for team members.
[05:36] Sophie: we support SSO/SAML for accounts beyond self-serve — for trial you'll get standard account invites, but we can enable SSO for pilot orgs if needed. RBAC is available in the console.

Demo requests and artifacts
[05:48] Tom: can you send a minimal perf test we can run against hosted to measure p95 and concurrency?
[05:53] Ravi: yes i'll attach a small benchmark script (go/python) and a spreadsheet to record p50/p95 and token counts. we'll include suggested payload sizes and sequence length.
[06:05] Maya: also send the quickstart repo and an example prompt set so we can sanity check quality.

Pricing & contract questions
[06:15] Maya: if we start hosted and later move to Dedicated, how does billing work?
[06:19] Sophie: hosted is usage-based. Dedicated is reserved capacity with commitments; we can offset credits against first month in some cases. we'll put together a transition playbook.

Risk & objections
[06:30] Jada: main risk from our side is auditability and key control. we need to see the SOC2 and understand KMS options.
[06:36] Sophie: understood — i'll get the SOC2 and a KMS architecture note over. for pilot we can also redact PII or avoid logging full payloads if needed.

Wrap-up and recap
[06:50] Sophie: to recap — action items: i'll spin up a trial org and send 60 credits, ravi will share quickstart and perf scripts, and jada will send us a short list of required audit fields. if everyone is good we can tentatively schedule an infra deep-dive next week.
[07:10] Maya: sounds good, let's aim for the deep-dive on 7/13.
[07:14] Tom: works for me.
[07:16] Jada: ok will send audit list by monday.

Action items (in-transcript):
[07:25] - Sophie: create org + invite, attach credits
[07:28] - Ravi: send perf scripts and quickstart repo link
[07:31] - Jada: list of audit log fields + retention req

Closing
[07:40] Sophie: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet. if anything else comes up email me or drop in the shared slack channel.
[07:46] Maya: thanks, bye.
[07:48] Tom: bye.
[07:50] Jada: bye.

Notes on transcription quality: automated notes occasionally mistranscribe product names (Redwood Dedi vs Dedicated), and technical terms like 'KV cache' may appear as 'KV cash' or 'K-V cash' in the automated text. Speakers sometimes overlap so labels may shift.
